inc-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts from Private/VPC customers in us-west-2 -> rolling spike since 02:07 UTC, rate: 4.2% 5xx across private routes, alerts from healthchecks and API gateway. Pager triggered (P1).

maria (oncall-sre): I'm paged, jumping in. any initial triage notes?

sam (eng-platform): Seeing repeated 504s at the gateway for private customers. Dashboards show latency and timeouts on egress to model-serving nodes.

maria (oncall-sre): Are these all in the same VPC peering / NAT path?

sam (eng-platform): Mostly private deployments with NAT gateway and peering to our shared serving fleet. Affected tenants: ~8 customers, all private.

lee (networking): I can repro a large number of TCP RSTs and conntrack drops on the edge NAT instances. Looks like conntrack exhausted.

kyle (oncall-ecs): If conntrack is full, new connections get dropped and load balancers return 502/504. Could explain gateway errors/timeouts.

maria (oncall-sre): Good call. Can you dump the conntrack counts? Also any recent security group or route updates?

lee (networking): Running on a NAT host now: ```
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
123450
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
131072
# cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l
122900
```

lee (networking): Count is > 94% of max, churn high. No recent SG changes on our side in last 2 hours per audit.

maria (oncall-sre): Okay. Do we have autoscaling for NAT hosts? If not, we should add capacity and reduce conntrack pressure.

sam (eng-platform): NATs are in an autoscaling group but scale policies didn't trigger because CPU is low — it's conntrack saturation, not CPU. Scale by adding more NAT instances manually.

kyle (oncall-ecs): I'm starting an emergency scale + adding a temporary iptables conntrack timeout tweak to reduce table pressure. Will also schedule a rolling replace of NATs.

maria (oncall-sre): Please list exact steps you plan. Also we need a customer impact blurb for CS. jenn, FYI.

kyle (oncall-ecs): Plan: 1) Launch 3 new NAT instances in the affected subnet. 2) Update route table weight / attach new NATs. 3) Tune conntrack: set nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=600 -> 300 temporarily. 4) Increase nf_conntrack_max to 262144 as short-term. 5) Monitor errors.

lee (networking): I have the commands ready: ```
# sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
# sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300
# iptables -t raw -A PREROUTING -p tcp -m tcp --syn -j CT --notrack
``` Note: last rule is risky, will only apply if we see sustained emergency levels.

maria (oncall-sre): Let's avoid aggressive iptables changes unless necessary. Proceed with 1-3 first and monitor. kyle, start launching NATs now.

kyle (oncall-ecs): Launching + tagging as emergency-scale-176418. ETA ~ 3 minutes to attach and drain.

sam (eng-platform): I'm preparing a failover: route private traffic to secondary region fallback for the most impacted tenants if errors persist. Need explicit approval before cross-region routing.

jenn (customer-success): Heads up for comms: Affected customers are on private plan, I've opened a ticket with the 8 tenants and posted an initial advisory — they want ETA. I'll share updates as we have them.

lee (networking): New NAT instances are up, attaching to route table now.

kyle (oncall-ecs): NATs attached, conntrack_pressure should drop once connections rebalance. Running: ```
# sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 262144
```

maria (oncall-sre): Applying tcp timeout tweak now (temporary). ```
# sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established = 300
```

sam (eng-platform): Watching the graphs — 5xx rate is already trending down from 4.2% -> 1.1% over the last 4 minutes. Latency tail improving.

lee (networking): conntrack count dropped to ~60k after new NATs and timeout tweak. ```
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
61234
```

maria (oncall-sre): Nice. Keep monitoring for 30m. Do we need to make any SG/peering changes?

lee (networking): No SG changes. Root cause likely connection storm from model-serving retries + long-lived connections exhausting conntrack. We'll follow up with traffic analysis, but immediate mitigation stable.

jenn (customer-success): Sending update to affected customers: short outage/timeouts for private deployments, mitigated by scaling NAT and conntrack tuning. ETA for full verification: 30–60 min.

sam (eng-platform): Postmortem action items I propose: 1) Make conntrack a metric with alerting at 70% threshold. 2) Add proactive autoscale trigger based on conntrack usage. 3) Harden retry/backoff behavior on serving clients.

maria (oncall-sre): Agreed. I'll file the incident ticket and assign action items. Severity P1 -> downgraded to P2 for follow-up since customer impact reduced.

kyle (oncall-ecs): I'll leave the sysctl changes in place for 1 hour then revert if stable. Also schedule rolling NAT replacement with larger instance types.

lee (networking): I'll collect tcpdump slices and correlate source IPs to tenant ids for the postmortem. Exporting capture now.

maria (oncall-sre): Thanks everyone. final note for timeline: detected 02:07 UTC, mitigation (scale + sysctl) in place 02:13 UTC, error rate back to baseline by 02:20 UTC. Will post full incident writeup in #postmortems.

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: P1 -> P2. Root cause suspected: conntrack exhaustion on NAT hosts causing dropped connections -> gateway 5xx/timeouts. Mitigation: emergency scale + conntrack tuning. Next: postmortem and metric/alert work scheduled.
